Claude CodevsHagiCode

What it is

Anthropic's agentic coding tool; one engine behind the CLI, IDE extensions, desktop app and web

Desktop and web workbench that runs Agent CLIs, Claude Code among them; not a model or an agent itself

Pricing and licensing

Needs a Pro ($20 per month), Max (from $100), Team or Enterprise plan, a Console account, or Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry; free claude.ai plan excluded (as of October 2026)

Desktop and Container editions are free; Store edition is free with an optional one-time TurboEngine purchase

Parallel work

Subagents, plus background agents to run several sessions and watch them from one screen

Several sessions side by side, each an Agent with a visible status, across any Agent CLI

Spec and planning workflow

Plan mode, CLAUDE.md memory, skills and hooks; no proposal archive of its own

OpenSpec proposals: propose, validate, apply, archive; free editions allow 3 concurrent proposals

Every change follows the same three steps

No open-ended chat threads. Each change becomes a proposal you can review, a run you can trace, and knowledge you can reuse.

  1. Proposal

    Describe the change. Hagicode checks your repository and drafts a proposal with specs and tasks you can read and correct before any code is touched.

    • proposal.md
    • design.md
    • tasks.md

  2. Execution

    Approve the plan and agents carry it out task by task, in parallel across Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot and more, ticking each task off as it lands.

    • tasks.md

  3. Archive

    Finished changes are archived back into your specs. The next proposal reads them first, so it starts from what the team already learned.

    • specs/
Archive feeds the next proposal

Built for real development work

Proposals keep every change reviewable; parallel agents keep the work moving

Smart

Propose first, execute second: every change leaves a trail

What each change leaves behind01 / 08 · Review
  • openspec/specs/
  • openspec/changes/<change-id>/
  • proposal.md
  • design.md
  • tasks.md
  • specs/<capability>/spec.md
  • $ openspec validate --strict
  • openspec/changes/archive/

HagiCode doesn't just chat about your code. It reviews the real project state, writes a proposal and spec deltas, validates them strictly, runs the tasks in order, then archives what it learned for the next change.

Efficient

Run many agents and instances in parallel so your quota never sits idle

One at a time, waiting in line
Side by side, none waiting on another

Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode, Hermes and the other supported Agent CLIs can each run several instances at once. Proposals, fixes and reviews get their own lane, so one slow result never stalls the rest.
